3DES.pad_amount_detail: All 8 plaintext lengths are multiples of block_size=8, so padding is always exactly 8 bytes (1 block). The 5 padding schemes produce different byte patterns but identical padding length.
3DES.padding_scheme_note: 5 schemes used (PKCS7, ISO10126, ANSI_X923, Zero, Random) — content varies but length does not

AES-256.padding_scheme_note: 5 schemes used — content varies but length does not

DES.pad_amount_detail: All 8 plaintext lengths are multiples of block_size=8, so padding is always exactly 8 bytes (1 block).
DES.padding_scheme_note: 5 schemes used — content varies but length does not

ChaCha20.pad_amount_detail: Stream cipher — no padding. CT length = PT length. 8 unique plaintext lengths confirms PT length varies.

RSA-2048.pad_amount_detail: PKCS#1 v1.5 padding — always pads to key size (256 bytes). CT length is constant; PT length varies (5 unique values).
RSA-2048.padding_scheme_note: PKCS1v15 used for both openssl and pycryptodome implementations

ML-KEM-768.pad_amount_detail: KEM encapsulation — CT is always 1088 bytes (fixed by ML-KEM-768 spec), shared secret is always 32 bytes. No padding concept applies.
ML-KEM-768.nonce_note: Implicit random coins per encapsulation call

fail_reason: Block cipher families (DES, 3DES, AES-128, AES-256): padding amount is CONSTANT within each family because all chosen plaintext lengths are exact multiples of the block size. The generation script uses PLAINTEXT_LENGTHS=[128,256,512,768,1024,2048,4096,8192] which are all divisible by 8 and 16. Pad byte *content* varies across 5 schemes but pad *length* does not vary. Reviewer #4's concern about padding diversity is valid for block cipher families.
recommendation: Regenerate v2 corpus with non-block-aligned plaintext lengths so padding amounts genuinely vary. Need plaintext lengths where len % block_size != 0 for block cipher families.
